model_annotation: The plot illustrates how training loss changes over optimization iterations for six methods/variants (Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64, H/T), and SepLLM (n=128)) shown as colored line traces. The x-axis is labeled “#Iteration,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 140,000 with regularly spaced tick labels every 20,000. The y-axis is labeled “Loss,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 with tick labels at 0.1 intervals. All series are drawn as solid lines without visible point markers and include faint surrounding variation bands; each curve starts near the top of the axis (around 3.4 at iteration 0), drops steeply within the early iterations, and then declines more gradually. The Vanilla line (light purple) falls from about 3.4 at 0 to roughly 2.70 by ~20,000 and continues down to about 2.50 by 140,000. The StrmLLM (n=64) line (blue) decreases from about 3.4 at 0 to roughly 2.82 by ~20,000 and then tapers to about 2.61 at 140,000. The SepLLM (n=64) line (orange) drops from about 3.4 at 0 to around 2.73 by ~20,000 and ends near 2.52 at 140,000. The SepLLM (n=64, H) line (green) follows a similar shape, moving from about 3.4 at 0 to around 2.72 by ~20,000 and reaching approximately 2.51 at 140,000. The SepLLM (n=64, H/T) line (red) declines from about 3.4 at 0 to roughly 2.69 by ~20,000 and finishes near 2.49 at 140,000. The SepLLM (n=128) line (dark purple/indigo) also drops sharply from about 3.4 at 0 to around 2.68 by ~20,000 and continues downward to approximately 2.47–2.48 at 140,000.
